ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the circuit diagram, there are two vertical wires on the left and right as common terminals, and a battery is connected at the bottom. The upper horizontal branch has three identically shaped resistors connected in series from the left end to the right end; the marked point W is located between the first and second resistors, and the marked point U is located between the second and third resistors. The middle horizontal branch also has three identically shaped resistors connected in series from the left-side point T to the right-side point P; the marked point S is located between the first and second resistors, and the marked point Q is located between the second and third resistors. Reasoning: The problem states that all resistors have the same resistance, and the resistance of the voltmeter is very large, so connecting the voltmeter will not significantly change the current and potential distribution of the original circuit. The upper branch and the middle branch are both composed of three identical resistors connected in series, and they are connected between the same pair of left and right end nodes, so they are identical voltage dividers. In identical voltage dividers, the corresponding points after passing through the same number of resistors from the left end have the same potential. U is the point in the upper branch after passing through two resistors from the left end, and Q is the point in the middle branch after passing through two resistors from the left end, so U and Q have the same potential. A voltmeter connected between equipotential points has a reading of zero.

raw_record.question_text: In the circuit shown below, each of the resistors has the same resistance. A voltmeter with very high resistance is connected between two points in the circuit. Between which two points of connection would the voltmeter read zero?

method.method_draft: Use the visual symmetry of the two horizontal resistor chains. First read from the image that the top branch from the left rail to the right rail has three equal resistors in series with points W after the first resistor and U after the second; the middle branch from T to P also has three equal resistors in series with points S after the first resistor and Q after the second. From the text, use that all resistors have the same resistance and the voltmeter has very high resistance, so attaching it does not disturb the circuit. Since the top and middle branches are identical voltage dividers connected across the same two end nodes, corresponding points at the same fraction of the way across the divider are at the same potential. U and Q are both after two of the three equal resistors from the left side, so their potentials are equal. Therefore a voltmeter connected between Q and U reads zero.

method.method_draft: Assign potentials and calculate voltage drops. From the image, identify the left vertical rail containing T as one supply terminal and the right vertical rail containing P as the other, with both the upper and middle branches connected between these same terminals. Each branch has three equal resistors in series; Q and U are each located between the second and third resistors counting from the left. From the text, take each resistor as resistance R and ignore the voltmeter current because its resistance is very high. If the supply voltage between the left and right rails is V, then each three-resistor branch has total resistance 3R and the same current V/(3R). The voltage drop across each resistor in either branch is V/3. Thus the potential at U is the left-rail potential minus 2V/3, and the potential at Q is also the left-rail potential minus 2V/3. Their potential difference is zero, so the voltmeter reads zero between Q and U.

Between these same two rails there are two horizontal branches. The upper branch has three identical resistors in series, with W between the first and second resistors and U between the second and third resistors. The middle branch also has three identical resistors in series, with S between the first and second resistors and Q between the second and third resistors.

Reasoning: Let each resistor have resistance R. Because the voltmeter has very high resistance, it draws negligible current and does not change the circuit. The upper and middle branches are both connected across the same supply voltage between the left and right rails, so each branch has total resistance 3R. The voltage drop across each resistor in either branch is therefore one third of the rail-to-rail voltage. Points U and Q are in corresponding positions: each is after two equal resistor voltage drops from the left rail. Thus U and Q have the same electric potential, so the potential difference between them is zero.
